title: eval-harness: CI gating for prompt-set regression and quality metric integrations
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: We need automated, enforceable checks for prompt-set regressions and quality metric regressions as part of PR validation. This change adds an optional CI gating step that runs a lightweight eval against the project's canonical prompt-sets and blocks merges when a predefined quality delta threshold is exceeded. The goal is to catch unintended quality regressions early without adding large latency to CI. What changed: 1) CI: new GitHub Actions workflow .github/workflows/eval-gate.yml that runs a fast eval job on a representative subset of prompts and reports aggregated metrics (exact-match, BLEU, and our custom semantic-acceptance score). 2) Eval harness: new gating mode (--ci-gate) that runs minimal sampling, uses cached model artifacts when available, and emits machine-readable metric outputs (JSON) and a compact summary for PR comments. 3) Metrics integration: added a small metrics module that compares current run to baseline and returns a pass/fail status based on config thresholds (config/eval-gates.yaml). 4) Dev UX: a lightweight action reports results back to the PR as a status check and summary comment; opt-in gating configured per-repo. 5) Tests & docs: unit tests for gating logic, end-to-end smoke test in CI, and docs/ci.md describing how to opt in and tune thresholds. Rollout plan: default state is opt-in via repo config; repo-admins can enable gating for protected branches. For Redwood monorepo testing, we will enable gating on the eval-harness repo and pilot on redwood/services-inference. Checklist: - [x] Add GH Action workflow file - [x] Implement --ci-gate mode in harness - [x] Add metric comparator and baseline storage format - [x] Add PR comment/status integration - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs and rollout notes Related work: ENG-5592 (quality gates design), ENG-5640 (CI integration spike). Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the eval sample small (<=50 prompts) to keep runtime under 8 minutes on CI runners. Larger nightly jobs will continue to run the full evals and update baselines. The gate is conservative by default (0.5% relative drop on core semantic-acceptance score) and configurable in eval-gates.yaml.

Jade Thompson: Could we surface per-prompt deltas in the PR comment for faster triage?
Priya Nair: Added compact per-prompt table when --verbose-gate is enabled; default remains summary-only to keep comment size small.
Marco Li: CI runtime looks within budget on linux runners, but let's gate GPU-heavy tests to nightly. Approved after small nits.
release_notes: Add optional CI gating for prompt-set regressions and quality metric integrations. Opt-in via config/eval-gates.yaml; default conservative thresholds recommended.
notes: This is an opt-in gate. Repository admins should review configuration and baseline storage before enabling on protected branches.
